abstract_sentences.text: Randomized self-reductions (RSRs) express f(x) using f evaluated at random correlated points, enabling self-correcting programs, instance-hiding protocols, and applications in complexity theory and cryptography.
abstract_sentences.transition: Opens with object, mechanism, and applications before the gap.

evidence.anchor: express f(x) using f evaluated at random correlated points

abstract_sentences.text: Yet discovering RSRs has required manual expert derivation for over 40 years, limiting their practical use.
abstract_sentences.comparison: manual expert derivation versus desired practical use
abstract_sentences.transition: Contrasts the established applications with a discovery bottleneck.

evidence.anchor: manual expert derivation for over 40 years

abstract_sentences.text: We present Bitween for automated RSR learning.
abstract_sentences.transition: Names the proposed response before its three-part expansion.

abstract_sentences.text: First, we formalize RSR learning with sample complexity analysis under correlated sampling.
abstract_sentences.transition: First contribution; opens the theory branch.

evidence.anchor: sample complexity analysis under correlated sampling

abstract_sentences.text: Second, we develop Vanilla Bitween, which integrates multiple backends (linear regression, genetic programming, symbolic regression, and mixed-integer programming).
abstract_sentences.transition: Second contribution; sets up the backend comparison in the next sentence.

abstract_sentences.text: The linear regression backend outperforms the others, discovering RSRs for 43 of 80 functions (54%) in RSR-Bench, our benchmark suite, including the first known reduction for sigmoid.
abstract_sentences.comparison: linear regression backend versus the other Vanilla backends
abstract_sentences.transition: Closes the Vanilla branch and precedes Agentic Bitween.

abstract_sentences.text: Third, we introduce Agentic Bitween, a neuro-symbolic approach where LLM agents propose novel query functions beyond the fixed set (x+r, x-r, x*r, x, r) in prior work.
abstract_sentences.comparison: novel queries versus the fixed prior set
abstract_sentences.transition: Third contribution; prepares the final quantitative result.

abstract_sentences.text: Agentic Bitween discovers RSRs for 64 of 80 functions (80%), outperforming pure neural baselines in both RSR discovery and verification accuracy.
abstract_sentences.comparison: Agentic Bitween versus pure neural baselines
abstract_sentences.transition: Terminal sentence and strongest abstract claim.

introduction_moves.answer: Establishes RSRs as a useful theoretical object with cryptographic, self-correcting, instance-hiding, checking, and proof applications.
introduction_moves.next_hook: If RSRs are useful, why are they not broadly discovered?

introduction_moves.unresolved_from_previous: Practical availability of known RSR applications.
introduction_moves.answer: Says prior work depended on expert derivation and five fixed query functions, leaving many transformations unreachable.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Construct a hypothesis space with suitable queries and algebraic relationships.

evidence.anchor: limited to a handful of fixed query functions

introduction_moves.unresolved_from_previous: How can the query/hypothesis-space bottleneck be operationalized?
introduction_moves.answer: Introduces Bitween's random sampling, regression, heuristics, verification, and the split between Vanilla and Agentic variants.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Benchmarks/backend comparison and pure-neural comparison motivate explicit contributions.

introduction_moves.unresolved_from_previous: What exactly must be delivered by the framework?
introduction_moves.answer: Lists theory, V-B backend comparison, A-B novel query generation, 80-function/8-category RSR-Bench, and non-scalar generalization.
introduction_moves.next_hook: The sigmoid motivating example makes the abstract system concrete.

experimental_design.name: Contribution-oriented evaluation objective
experimental_design.description: Section 6 says the evaluation validates fixed-query LR suitability and Agentic Bitween's novel-query discovery; it does not enumerate preregistered research questions or decision thresholds.

evidence.anchor: two key contributions outlined in Section 1

experimental_design.name: RSR-Bench task population
experimental_design.description: The main suite contains 80 continuous real-valued scientific and ML functions in eight categories, with some ground-truth properties sourced from self-testing and functional-equation literature.

experimental_design.name: Methods and baselines
experimental_design.description: Evaluates four V-B backends, A-B with GPT-OSS-120B/Claude-Sonnet-4/Claude-Opus-4.1, and same-model N-Research agents with only sequential thinking.

experimental_design.name: Sampling, budget, and hardware
experimental_design.description: Main text specifies uniform sampling in [-10,10], δ=0.001, five repeats, 1800 s timeout, 32GB Apple M1 Pro; Appendix Table 3 specifies generally 30 samples, 80/20 train-test, degree 2 or 3, and denominator cap 20.

experimental_design.name: Tuning and implementation detail
experimental_design.description: Appendix E gives five-fold CV/grid-search and backend configurations; Appendix F prints the agent system prompt and two tool instructions.

experimental_design.name: Non-scalar extension design
experimental_design.description: A separate 17-function algebraic set flattens multidimensional inputs and uses the same 1800 s timeout; results are reported separately from RSR-Bench.

evidence.anchor: 17 functions drawn from non-scalar algebraic structures

experimental_design.name: Excluded recent backends
experimental_design.description: RAG-SR, MetaSymNet, and ParFam were integrated but excluded from the principal evaluation after timeouts, crashes, or limited verified properties under tried settings.

evidence.anchor: do not include them in the evaluation

result_inventory.claim: Within the fixed query class, V-B ITWEEN-LR is the strongest reported Vanilla backend.
result_inventory.value: Table 1: 87/87|46 RSR/verified|unverified, 54% coverage, 0|5|19 s runtime; abstract summarizes discovery on 43/80 functions (54%).
result_inventory.comparison: Versus PySR 61/61|60 at 38%, GPLearn 48/48|54 at 32%, and MILP 74/74|29 at 51% coverage.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate counts, benchmark-level coverage, and min|average|max runtime; five repeats stated elsewhere, without reported dispersion or hypothesis test.

result_inventory.claim: A-B ITWEEN with Claude Opus 4.1 has the highest reported main-benchmark coverage.
result_inventory.value: Table 1: 793/1628|26 and 80% coverage; abstract reports RSRs for 64/80 functions (80%).
result_inventory.comparison: Versus N-Research Claude Opus 4.1 at 250/539|172 and 64% coverage, and other A-B models at 59% and 66% coverage.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate counts/coverage/runtime, with manually confirmed RSR subset; no error bars or test reported in Table 1.

result_inventory.claim: Novel query functions expand the form of discovered properties beyond the fixed set.
result_inventory.value: Table 2 gives sigmoid x+log(k), modulo compositions, Gudermannian, softmax, inverse, Gaussian, sinh, tanh, and exp(sin x) examples; text names 23 functions with no V-B LR verified RSRs and up to 33 A-B Opus RSRs per function.
result_inventory.comparison: Fixed-query V-B LR versus A-B novel-query results.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Representative formula table plus a reported count over 23 functions; no per-query causal decomposition.

result_inventory.claim: The paper associates tool use with more discovered properties and fewer unverified properties.
result_inventory.value: Figure 3 shows per-benchmark tool calls; the text identifies A-B Claude Opus 4.1 as using both tools more, while Table 1 reports 26 unverified properties versus 172 for N-Research Claude Opus 4.1.
result_inventory.comparison: A-B tool-equipped agent versus N-Research agent using only sequential thinking with the same model family.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Heatmap and aggregate false-positive counts; association, not an isolated per-tool intervention.

result_inventory.claim: Agentic tool use carries a reported runtime and token cost.
result_inventory.value: A-B runtime is described as roughly 1.2–1.8× N-Research using the same model; token use roughly 2.8–3.5×.
result_inventory.comparison: A-B versus N-Research for the same LLM.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Per-benchmark heatmaps and descriptive ratios; no uncertainty intervals reported.

result_inventory.claim: The pipeline has reported non-scalar breadth under a separate benchmark.
result_inventory.value: A-B Claude Opus 4.1 finds verified RSRs on 17/17 algebraic benchmarks, 170 RSRs out of 371 verified properties; V-B LR returns 12 RSRs across 11/17.
result_inventory.comparison: A-B Claude Opus 4.1 versus fixed-query V-B LR on 17 functions, separate from RSR-Bench.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate property counts, coverage, time, and tokens in Table 7, backed by detailed Tables 16–21.

ablation_inventory.name: Fixed-query backend comparison
ablation_inventory.description: V-B ITWEEN compares LR/Ridge/Lasso, MILP, PySR, and GPLearn under the fixed query-function paradigm; it identifies backend suitability rather than deleting an internal component.

ablation_inventory.name: Tool-access system contrast
ablation_inventory.description: N-Research uses only sequential thinking, whereas A-B has inference and symbolic verification tools; Figure 3/Table 1 provide mechanism-oriented system evidence but do not isolate one tool at a time.

ablation_inventory.name: Fixed versus novel query contrast
ablation_inventory.description: Table 2 directly juxtaposes V-B LR fixed-query RSRs with A-B novel-query RSRs; it is a representation-space comparison, not a randomized per-query ablation.

ablation_inventory.name: Dedicated component-deletion ablation
ablation_inventory.description: No separately titled ablation section or experiment removes inference, verification, query proposal, or sequential thinking one at a time while holding the rest fixed.

claim_closure.claim: Provide a rigorous framework for learning RSRs under correlated samples.
claim_closure.method_response: Maps Π, Q, d, and correlated samples into a learning pipeline.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Definitions 4.1/4.3/4.5, Fact 4.2, and Claims A.1–A.2 make the stated framework explicit.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls Bitween the first systematic approach for learning RSRs.

claim_closure.claim: LR is the most suitable fixed-query backend for RSR-Bench.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1, Figure 2, and Tables 8–9 provide aggregate/category/per-function comparisons.

claim_closure.claim: Agentic Bitween discovers novel queries and improves main-benchmark RSR coverage.
claim_closure.method_response: LLMs receive inference, symbolic-verification, and sequential-thinking tools.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1/2, Figure 3, Tables 10–15, and Table 20 report coverage and novel forms.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls the query discovery a paradigm shift.

claim_closure.claim: RSR-Bench is a comprehensive 80-function, eight-category benchmark.
claim_closure.method_response: Defines the benchmark and category membership.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 and Tables 5–15 enumerate categories and per-function outcomes.

claim_closure.claim: The framework generalizes without architectural changes to non-scalar algebraic structures.
claim_closure.method_response: Flattens inputs while retaining the inference and verification tools.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 7 and Tables 16–21 report results on 17 selected functions.

claim_closure.method_response: Candidate generation and symbolic verification are automated in the pipeline.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The reported RSR count is a manually confirmed subset of verified properties, leaving a human confirmation stage for the reported metric.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion uses automated-discovery language without separately resolving the manual subset boundary.

limitations.name: Redundant discovered properties
limitations.description: Some discovered RSR properties may be algebraically derivable from others; the authors did not apply Gröbner-basis reduction because of its stated computational cost.

limitations.name: Discovery incompleteness
limitations.description: No discovered RSR does not imply non-existence; the search is constrained by query-space infinity, precision, sampling, and degree 2–3.

evidence.anchor: absence of discovered RSRs does not imply non-existence

limitations.name: Agentic computational cost
limitations.description: A-B has increased runtime and token use versus pure neural methods because of iterative tool interactions.

limitations.name: Recent backend exclusions
limitations.description: RAG-SR, MetaSymNet, and ParFam are not included in the evaluated comparison after the failure modes reported in Section 5.

evidence.anchor: do not include them in the evaluation

limitations.name: Algebraic-scope caveat
limitations.description: Algebraic results hold for the specific benchmark implementations and omit several natural follow-up structures.

limitations.name: Manual boundary for reported RSRs
limitations.description: Table 1 defines reported RSRs as a manually confirmed subset of verified properties and says some may still have been missed.

evidence.anchor: we might still have missed some

limitations.name: Reported uncertainty
limitations.description: The paper states five repetitions but the visible aggregate results do not report dispersion, interval estimates, or a named significance test.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Manual confirmation is disclosed rather than hidden
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: The RSR metric selects a manually confirmed subset of automatically verified properties; this is a denominator/curation boundary, not an inference about author motive.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Detailed outcomes migrate to appendix
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: Main text foregrounds Table 1/2 and Figures 2–4; per-function outcomes and full properties appear in Tables 8–21. This is a layout fact, not a claim of intent.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Direct positive discussion of adverse evidence
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: Backend failures, manual filtering, redundancy, incompleteness, and cost are explicitly named in method/results/limitations rather than being absent from the narrative.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Intentional concealment
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: The PDF supplies no evidence that appendix placement, aggregation, or metric choices were intended to conceal adverse results; no such intent is inferred here.

measurement_disagreements.name: Abstract coverage versus Table 1 total RSR count
measurement_disagreements.description: No contradiction: 43/80 and 64/80 are function-level coverage statements, while 87 and 793 in Table 1 are cumulative RSR counts under the table's RSR/verified|unverified format.

measurement_disagreements.name: 15-sample sigmoid example versus general 30-sample setting
measurement_disagreements.description: No contradiction: p.2 calls 15 samples the motivating sigmoid example, while Appendix Table 3 gives n=30 as a shared evaluation setting.

measurement_disagreements.name: Automatic measurement draft
measurement_disagreements.description: No automatic measurement draft was supplied with the assigned paper package, so there is no draft-versus-PDF disagreement to correct.

measurement_disagreements.name: Text-extraction spacing
measurement_disagreements.description: The visual PDF uses spaced small caps such as B ITWEEN and N-R ESEARCH. Raw extraction can split these names; lexical counting should normalize them and exclude formula/table tokens.

final_judgment.single_storyline: The paper frames automated RSR discovery as a search-space problem: fixed-query correlated-sample regression discovers only part of the space; LLM-proposed queries plus inference/verification tools expand it while retaining symbolic validation. [p.1 §1, explicit, “fixed query functions”; p.6 §5, explicit, “dynamically propose novel query functions”; p.7–8 Tables 1–2, explicit, “Novel-query RSRs”]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the formal target, Algorithm 1, backend/tool design, 80-function aggregate counts/coverage/time, representative novel queries, tool-use/cost figures, and limitations. [p.5 Algorithm 1, explicit, “modulo regression”; p.7 Table 1, explicit, “rsr coverage”; p.9 Limitations, explicit, “increased runtime and token usage”]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, hyperparameters, full prompts/tool instructions, category membership, per-function metrics, and complete property catalogs move to Appendix A–H and Tables 8–21. The main decision claims remain readable, but reproducibility and property-level audit require the appendix. [p.14–23, layout_observation, “Experimental Hyperparameters”; p.24–78, layout_observation, “Detailed results”]
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest presentation pattern is concrete sigmoid RSR → explicit algorithm → aggregate Table 1 → representative novel-query Table 2 → tool/cost figures → full appendix catalog. [p.2 Eq. (1), explicit, “sigmoid function satisfies Equation (1)”; p.5 Algorithm 1, explicit, “V-B ITWEEN modulo regression”; p.34–78, layout_observation, “Discovered RSR Properties”]
final_judgment.largest_gap: Reported RSR counts retain a manual-confirmation boundary; five repetitions are stated without visible dispersion/testing, and A-B versus N-Research is a system-level tool-access contrast rather than a per-tool intervention. [p.7 Table 1, explicit, “manually confirmed subset”; p.6 Configuration, explicit, “repeated 5 times”; p.6 §5, explicit, “access only to the sequential_thinking_tool”]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For an open candidate space with a formal verifier, stage expressive generation before constrained verification; report the aggregate decision evidence in the body and preserve candidate-level audit trails in an appendix.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule is limited when verification is incomplete, reported outcomes require human confirmation, or the benchmark does not represent the target distribution; then report curation criteria, failure rate, repeat-level variation, and scope. [p.7 §6, explicit, “manually filtered”; p.9 Limitations, explicit, “inherently incomplete”; p.23 Appendix H, explicit, “specific implementations”]
